classification.difficultyReason: Compare coefficients, select the fourth-quadrant auxiliary angle and solve the resulting cosine equation within the stated domain.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express $\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x$ in the form $A\cos(x+\theta)$, where $A>0$ and $0<\theta<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x&=A\cos x\cos\theta-A\sin x\sin\theta\end{aligned}$$
Comparing coefficients gives $A\cos\theta=\sqrt3$ and $A\sin\theta=-1$.
$$\begin{aligned}A^2&=(\sqrt3)^2+(-1)^2=4\\A&=2\\\tan\theta&=-\frac1{\sqrt3}\end{aligned}$$
Since $\cos\theta>0$ and $\sin\theta<0$, $\theta$ is in quadrant IV.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=2\pi-\frac\pi6=\frac{11\pi}{6}\\\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x&=2\cos\left(x+\frac{11\pi}{6}\right)\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence solve $\sqrt3\cos x+\sin x=1$, for $0\leq x<2\pi$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}2\cos\left(x+\frac{11\pi}{6}\right)&=1\\\cos\left(x+\frac{11\pi}{6}\right)&=\frac12\\x+\frac{11\pi}{6}&=\frac\pi3,\ \frac{5\pi}{3},\ \frac{7\pi}{3},\ \frac{11\pi}{3}\\x&=-\frac{3\pi}{2},\ -\frac\pi6,\ \frac\pi2,\ \frac{11\pi}{6}\end{aligned}$$
Reject $-\frac{3\pi}{2}$ and $-\frac\pi6$ because they lie outside $0\leq x<2\pi$.
$$x=\frac\pi2\text{ or }\frac{11\pi}{6}.$$
